title: The design signature and the natural designers
statement: The corpus engages the design-inference debate on a distinctive footing: it takes seriously the intuition that cellular life carries signatures of engineering (the intuition Meyer's programme argues and Dawkins conceded as a hypothetical), while rejecting the supernatural designer of the intelligent-design movement — the canon's designers are natural, evolved elsewhere, themselves created (woh-claim-0030), and empirically formulable in the way Crick and Orgel's directed panspermia showed; the corpus's claim is that this position is coherent and stateable, and that its truth would require exactly the kind of biological evidence that has not been produced.

includes: The position statement: natural, non-supernatural designers as a third option between the ID movement's designer and unguided abiogenesis — with the created-creators chain (woh-claim-0030) absorbing the regress objection Dawkins raised in the moment the article anchors on

The formulability layer: directed panspermia as the peer-reviewed demonstration that a created-life hypothesis can be scientifically stated (formulability, never evidence — the epistemic principles' own example)
The engagement with Meyer at the article's hinge: what the signature argument would need to show, and where the corpus's position departs from the ID movement's
The honesty clause, which is the record's spine: no biological evidence currently discriminates designed from evolved terrestrial life, and the corpus says so
excludes: Any claim that design has been detected in terrestrial biology; the record asserts coherence and stateability, not detection
Endorsement of the ID movement's arguments, institutions, or designer
The synthetic-biology analogy as proof (minimal-genome engineering shows design is possible, not that it happened)
Probability arguments over abiogenesis, which the corpus does not model

source_references.locator: The canon's laboratory-creation account, whose designers this record characterizes as natural and created
Meyer's information-argument programme — the strongest statement of the signature intuition, engaged and departed from
Icarus 19 (1973): the scientific formulability of designed terrestrial life
The synthetic-genome work as possibility demonstration (design of life is an existing engineering practice)

alternatives.statement: Evolutionary biology explains the appearance of design; there is no signature to account for, and the intuition the position takes seriously is the illusion Darwin dissolved.
Natural designers who left no discriminating evidence are as untestable as supernatural ones; naturalizing the designer does not empiricize the claim.
Citing Crick-Orgel and synthetic biology borrows scientific respectability for a religious doctrine — the patronizing-parasitism critique applied to this exact move.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001 or woh-claim-0030 is revised or retired.
A discriminating biological test between designed and evolved terrestrial life is proposed and survives review — in either direction, this record must move.
Public prose begins asserting detection or endorsing ID-movement arguments, both of which this record excludes.
The article's Meyer engagement is revised at its hinge.
